newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait denies seeking rapprochement with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait denies seeking rapprochement with Iraq.

text.p: Kuwait has denied seeking to mend ties with former occupier Iraq or asking the head of the Arab Parliamentary Union to mediate, newspapers reported on Thursday.
Al-Seyassah quoted a foreign ministry official as saying that Kuwait did not send Secretary-General Galal Saeed a message on ties with Iraq or asked him to mediate.

After talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo, Saeed told reporters on Wednesday he had received letters from both Iraq and Kuwait "which asserted the willingness of both sides to open the issue of their relations".
"The Union decided to send an envoy during its last meeting (in May) and I will go to both countries next month on a reconciliation mission on behalf of the Union," Saeed added.
The speaker of the Kuwaiti parliament, Ahmad al-Saadoun, welcomed Saeed's visit but also denied that the assembly was even prepared to discuss the issue of ties with Iraq.

Kuwait, freed of the seven-month Iraqi occupation in the 1991 Gulf War, has turned down several offers to normalise ties with Arab states which were seen as Iraq sympathisers during the Gulf crisis. It often says that dealing with Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein was out of the question.
